tested_scope: Four lightweight repository-native freshness surfaces across branch-history rollback, ref-name reuse, and complete same-repository restore.
evidence: GitHub REST refs docs show refs are mutable and deletable, so current ref state is not a monotonic witness.

GitHub REST commits docs show commit listing starts from a supplied SHA/branch and defaults to the current default branch, so a rewound branch can hide newer reachable history from a stateless caller.
GitHub activity-view docs show force-push and branch-change history exists, but the docs used here do not establish a zero-entitlement API monotonic-retention or restore-survival contract.
GitHub repository Events is documented as non-real-time with roughly 30s to 6h latency, so absence cannot prove currentness.
GitHub audit-log API requires Enterprise Cloud and is rejected by the zero-finite-paid-entitlement gate.
inference_scope: No tested surface supplies the missing stateless freshness bit after complete same-domain rollback; this is a bounded documentation-backed classification, not a universal impossibility claim about every GitHub feature.
unresolved_child: Find a zero-entitlement Chat-accessible freshness authority outside the content/ref restore equivalence class, or a repository-native prevention policy that makes rollback itself impossible and cannot be rolled back with repository content.
